newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel opposition chief slams Netanyahu over Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israel opposition chief slams Netanyahu over Arafat.

text.p: The leader of Israel's parliamentary opposition blasted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday for his criticism of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after suicide bomb attacks that killed 13 people.

"Now they are trying to roll everything onto Arafat even before they know where the suicide attackers came from," Israel's Itim news agency quoted Labour Party chief Ehud Barak as saying to kibbutz leaders in Tel Aviv.

Barak, a former army chief of staff who was Netanyahu's commander in an elite commando unit, was quoted as saying the prime minister was "not responsible, not trustworthy, did not stand up to pressure" and that his rule was like "the leadership of a blind goat".

A leaflet issued in the name of the militant Islamic Hamas movement claimed responsibility for the twin suicide bombings at a Jerusalem market last Wednesday. Israeli and PLO officials say they are not sure of its authenticity.

Netanyahu told his cabinet on Sunday that Israel would not honour peace deals it signed with Arafat unless the Palestinian leader cracked down on militants. Israel has threatened to enter Palestinian territory to fight militants if Arafat does not act.
Palestinians say they have fought to curb the militants.

Israel suspended already dormant peace talks with the Palestinians as a result of the double bombing and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, barring tens of thousands of Palestinians from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.
Barak said: "We've learned the hard way that this government has no other way to prevent terror beforehand. This government is not serious."
He urged Netanyahu to "renew the trust between himself and the region's leadership" in order to more effectively fight militants opposed to the Middle East peace process.

Netanyahu later summoned Barak to his office. In a statement released after the meeting, Netanyahu's office said he had urged Barak to refrain from criticising the government at a time when national unity was required.

"The prime minister told...Barak that in these days it was correct to let the government act on the international level, particularly opposite Arafat, in particular when the prime minister is refraining from meetings with Arafat in order to press him to fulfil his commitment to fight terror," it said.
Israel Radio said Netanyahu also asked Barak to refrain from meeting Arafat. It said Barak refused. Barak met Arafat for the first time in his capacity as Labour leader on July 24.
